operating_notes.text: Telecom Products segment profit before tax and interest was ₹383 Cr in Q4FY26 against ₹4.52 Cr a year earlier, on segment revenue of ₹1,206.22 Cr.
Turnkey Contracts and Services segment posted a loss before tax and interest of ₹84.10 Cr in Q4FY26, against ₹56.43 Cr a year earlier.
The company recognised ₹8.91 Cr of past service cost on a consolidated basis in Q3FY26 under Employee benefit expense following the new Labour Codes.
HFCL is expanding optical fibre capacity to 33.9 mn fkm by December 2026 and setting up a preform manufacturing facility of 310 MTPA.
HFCL and HTL Limited won ~₹84.23 Cr (incl. GST) of optical fibre cable supply orders from a domestic private telecom operator, to be executed by August 2026.
FY26 export revenue was 41.36% of total, against 12.23% in FY25, with more than 70% of cable production exported.
Order book of ₹21,200 Cr includes ₹12,250 Cr of exports (58%) and ₹3,500 Cr of 6-7 year O&M contracts.
Optical fibre is at 100% utilisation; capacity is being raised from 28 mn fkm to 33.9 mn fkm by December 2026.
Secured export orders worth ~USD 19.32 million (~₹183.95 crore) for optical fiber cables, to be executed by August 2026.
Board approved setting up a Defence Manufacturing Facility in Andhra Pradesh with an outlay of ~₹230 crore to produce ~40 lakh units of Multi-Mode Hand Grenades by December 2027.
Export order of ~USD 11.07 million (~₹106.19 crore) for optical fiber cables from an unnamed international customer, through the overseas wholly owned subsidiary, to be executed by August 2026.

HFCL's corporate guarantee for HTL's working-capital facilities cut to ₹265 Cr (SBI ₹105 Cr, Yes Bank ₹115 Cr, Kotak Mahindra Bank ₹45 Cr) from ₹295 Cr; HFCL holds 74% of HTL, Government of India 26%.

25 May 2026: 7,50,00,000 warrants allotted at ₹74 each to NextWave Communications (Promoter, 3.75 Cr) and Satellite Finance (Promoter Group, 3.75 Cr); ₹138.75 Cr (25%) received, balance on conversion.

Secured a purchase order of ~₹135.09 crore (including GST) from RailTel Corporation of India Limited for an Annual Maintenance Contract of the Secure Operations Network for defence forces data centres, to be executed ending in January 2031.

As on 31 March 2026, 15.78% of HFCL equity was encumbered by non-disposal undertakings for securing the company's borrowings; MN Ventures pledged 50,00,000 shares (0.33%) and NextWave had 11,97,30,150 shares (7.82%) under NDU.
International fibre realisation is $18-28 per fibre km, with data-centre fibre at $22-28, and prices have risen significantly in the last six months.
Order book of ₹26,665 Cr includes ₹16,000 Cr of optical fibre cable and about ₹300 Cr of defence; ₹22,000 Cr is to be executed within five years.
Data-centre connectivity capacity, including subsidiary HTL, is being expanded 5x, with ₹850 Cr+ of orders in hand.
Order book exceeds ₹28,900 crore as of Q2FY27.

HFCL incorporated HFCL Connectivity Systems Limited (CIN U42202HR2026PLC152025) as a wholly owned subsidiary with ₹1 lakh capital, subscribing 1,00,000 shares of Re. 1 each; it is yet to commence business.

timeline.summary: On 24 April 2026, HFCL held an extraordinary general meeting where shareholders approved the preferential issue of securities.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,824.12 Cr (+127.8% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹178.5 Cr (against a loss of ₹81.43 Cr a year earlier).
HFCL released its investor presentation on April 30, 2026, guiding for over ₹10,000 Cr revenue and 20-21% EBITDA margin by FY29.
HFCL Q4FY26 monitoring agency reports show ₹478 Cr utilised out of ₹550 Cr QIP proceeds
Manoj Baid, President & Company Secretary, disclosed the Investors’/Analysts Conference Call recording on April 30, 2026, via HFCL’s website.

On 4 May 2026, HFCL and its material subsidiary HTL Limited secured purchase orders worth ~₹84.23 Cr (including GST) for supply of optical fibre cables from a leading private telecom operator, to be executed by August 2026.
HFCL's Q4FY26 call (transcript filed 8 May 2026) guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% and a 3-4 point margin rise, on a ₹21,200 Cr order book.
HFCL secured export orders worth ~₹183.95 crore for optical fiber cables on May 11, 2026.
On 14 May 2026, HFCL announced board approval to establish a greenfield defence manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh for ~₹230 crore to produce Multi-Mode Hand Grenades by December 2027.

On 16 May 2026, HFCL said its overseas wholly owned subsidiary secured an export order of ~USD 11.07 million (~₹106.19 crore) for optical fiber cables from an unnamed international customer, to be executed by August 2026.
On 19 May 2026, HFCL issued a ₹265 Cr corporate guarantee for its 74%-owned subsidiary HTL, replacing an earlier ₹295 Cr guarantee.

On 25 May 2026, HFCL allotted 7,50,00,000 warrants at ₹74 each to promoter-group entities NextWave Communications and Satellite Finance, receiving ₹138.75 Cr upfront (25%), with promoter-group holding to rise to 16.87% on full conversion.
HFCL secured a ₹135.09 crore AMC purchase order from RailTel Corporation of India Limited for the secure OPS network, to be executed by January 2031.
HFCL restructures defence business: invests ₹89.25 Cr in HASPL and acquires HDSPL
On 5 June 2026, HFCL's promoter group declared holding of 43,30,44,594 shares (28.29%) as on 31 March 2026, with 15.78% encumbered by non-disposal undertakings for the company's borrowings.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,541.79 Cr (+143.6% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹362.91 Cr (+434.8% YoY).
On October 19, 2026, HFCL released monitoring agency reports indicating ₹525.67 crore of QIP proceeds had been utilized.
HFCL Limited hosted the Investors'/Analysts Conference Call recording on October 19, 2026, available at https://www.hfcl.com/.
HFCL incorporated HFCL Connectivity Systems Limited as a 100% subsidiary on October 22, 2026, subscribing 1,00,000 shares of Re. 1 each for ₹1 lakh; the entity is yet to commence business.
